title: Electric Signs, Fund Transfers, Tax Corrections
summary:
Here's a summary of the Austin City agenda from June 12, 1913:

*   **New Financial Policy:** The city adopted a significant policy to transfer all interest earned from major funds (like those for sanitary sewers, street improvements, hospitals, and cemeteries) directly into its Interest and Sinking Fund, with over $1,000 transferred from May’s earnings.
*   **Public Space for Businesses:** Multiple permits were issued for electric signs extending over sidewalks on Congress Avenue for businesses, as well as a private staircase on San Jacinto Street, all subject to city revocation.
*   **Correcting Old Tax Records:** The council approved the correction or cancellation of several historical tax assessments for citizens, some dating back to 1895, due to errors in original property or personal levies.
*   **Key City Appointments:** Important city roles were filled, including the confirmation of a new Chief and officers for the Fire Department, and the appointment of two Assistant Engineers.

The following resolution was passed by the Council on the 12th of June, 1913, but was not
handed the Clerk until the morning of the 19th Inst ,hence it is recorded at this time. be
it resolved by the City Council of the City of Austin : That permit be and is hereby
granted to Felix Cherico to erect a skeleton Iron staircase not more than three feet wide
on the sidewalk on San Jacinto street south of 6th street ,for access to the second or
upper stories of a building about to be erected at said place.
Be it further resolved :
That said staircase must be erected not less than 25 feet from the property line off of
6th street at said building,located at the corner of San Jacinto and East 6th streets.
Be it further resolved :
That the work to be done under this permit is to be done under the supervision and with
the approval of the Supt of Streets and Public Improvements.
Be it further resolved :
That this permit is given and is to be held and accepted as revocable at the pleasure of
the City Council .
The resolution was adopted by the following vote : Yeas Mayor Wooldridge, Councilmen
Anthony, Bartholomew, Haynes & Powell 5 Nays none.

Approved, A P Wooldridge, Mayor.
The Council then recessed subject to call.

June 14th 1913.
The Council was called to order by the Mayor with all members present: The Mayor laid
before the Council an ordinance granting to Austin Dam and Suburban Railway Company the
right and permitting said Company to construct maintain and operate a Railroad Switch
track or turn out upon and across certain streets in the City of Austin,subject to certain
conditions.
The ordinance was read the first time and a motion made to suspend the rule and place it
on its secondreading, which motion prevailed by the following vote : Yeas Mayor
Wooldridge, Councilmen Anthony, Bartholomew, Haynes & Powell 5 Nays none.
The ordinance was read the second time and laid over for one week. The Council adjourned.
